'''Robert Guillaumont'''<ref>{{cite web|title=Who's who|url=https://www.whoswho.fr/bio/robert-guillaumont_6884|publication-date=}}</ref> (born 26 February 1933 in Lyon) is a French chemist and honorary professor at the [[University of Paris-Saclay]] in [[Orsay]] (1967-1998), Member of the [[French Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Académie des sciences|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Liste-des-membres-de-l-Academie-des-sciences-/-G/robert-guillaumont.html|publication-date=}}</ref>  and the [[French Academy of Technologies]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Académie des Technologies|url=https://www.academie-technologies.fr/blog/categories/publications-de-l-academie/posts/les-dechets-nucleaires|publication-date=}}</ref>

== Career ==
Robert Guillaumont is a specialist in [[radiochemistry]] and [[Actinide chemistry|actinide]] chemistry. He prepared his doctorate at the Institut radium de Paris, Curie Laboratory, [[Pierre and Marie Curie University|University of Paris VI]] (1966). He continued his research in this Institute and then at the Radiochemistry Laboratory of the Orsay {{ill|Institut de physique nucléaire d'Orsay|fr|lt=Institute of Nuclear Physics}} (1968–98), which he directed for twelve years (1979–90). He taught [[chemistry]]/[[radiochemistry]] at the University of Paris XI-Orsay (1967–98). His expertise covers the chemistry of the nuclear fuel cycle (from [[uranium]] mining to waste management and spent fuel reprocessing) and nuclear energy issues. He has been a member or chairman of numerous French and international committees dealing with the nuclear fuel cycle, nuclear energy, radioactive waste management and the synthesis and use of [[radionuclide]]s for medicine. He was a member of the National Commission for the Evaluation of Research on Nuclear Materials and Radioactive Waste<ref>{{cite web|title=CNE|url=https://www.cne2.fr|publication-date=}}</ref> (1994-2019).

== Research ==
Robert Guillaumont began his research in 1959 on the chemistry of [[protactinium]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Protactinium encyclopedie universalis|date=29 January 2025 |url=https://www.Universalis.fr/encyclopedie/protactinium/#i_o}}</ref> in solution. He showed that the electronic filling of the 5f underlay begins for this element. The UV absorption spectrum of Pa<sup>4+</sup> is typical of a 5f<sup>1</sup>6d<sup>1</sup> transition (Pa atom: 5f<sup>2</sup>6d<sup>1</sup>7s<sup>2</sup>). Together with his collaborators, he extended his methodology for studying the behaviour of radioelements in imponderable quantities to other actinides. The rest of his work can be linked to the common thread of the consequences of filling the atomic underlayer 5f on the physicochemical properties of [[Actinide|actinides]]. This filling plays an essential role in the behaviour of the 15 actinides, especially when these electrons are delocalized, from protactinium (Pa) to [[americium]] (Am). This results in a high richness of oxidation degrees of the first actinides (usually from 3 to 6) and in the manifestation of particular effects in the series (electronic states characterized by the quantum number J). Thus, he studied the [[Thermodynamics|thermodynamic]] consequences of the population of sublayer 5f on a series of solution complexes<ref>S. Hubert, M. Hussonnois, L Brillard, G. Goby et  R. Guillaumont, « Détermination simultanée de constantes de formation de complexes citrique de l'américium, du curium, du californium, de l'einsteinium et du fermium », ''Journal of Inorganic and Nuclear Chemistry'', 1974, 36 (10), <abbr>p.</abbr> 2361-2366</ref> (citric complexes of trivalent actinides from Am to [[fermium]] (Fm). He showed the existence of the "tetrad effect" for trivalent actinide complexes, an effect that reflects an extra-stabilization of the fundamental state of actinides for 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4 of the filling of the 5f underlay. After the [[curium]] (Cm), it is necessary, to carry out experiments, to synthesize isotopes of [[berkelium]] (Bk), [[Einsteinium|einstenium]] (Es) and Fm by nuclear reactions with particle accelerators,<ref>B. Désiré, M. Hussonnois, R. Guillaumont, « Détermination de la première constante d’hydrolyse de l’américium, du curium, du berkélium et du californium », ''CR Acad. Sci. Paris'', 1969, 269, <abbr>p.</abbr> 448-462</ref><ref>M. Hussonnois, S. Hubert, L. Aubin, R. Guillaumont, G. Boussières, « Determination de la première constante d’hydrolyse du fermium », ''Radiochemical and Radioanalytical Letters'', 1972, 10 (4), <abbr>p.</abbr> 231-23</ref><ref>M. Hussonnois, S. Hubert, L Brillard, R. Guillaumont, « Production et hydrolyse de l'einsteinium », ''Radiochem. Radioanal. Letters'', 1973, 15 (1), <abbr>p.</abbr> 47-56</ref> and separate them from irradiated targets, which he did at Orsay. To conduct most of his research he developed the methodology for studying species and equilibria between species in extremely diluted solutions (which radioactivity allows until about 10<sup>−14</sup> M), and he pushed, at the theoretical level, the description of the thermodynamic behaviour of a few atoms in terms of deviation from the [[law of mass action]],<ref>A. Peneloux, R. Guillaumont, « Solutions de dilution extrême et  loi d’action de masse », ''CR Acad. Sci. Paris'', 1990, 310 (12), <abbr>p.</abbr> 1607-1613</ref> which gave a foundation to chemical experiments on elements 6d (Z>103), produced atom by atom by radiochemists at accelerators.<ref>J.P. Adloff et R. Guillaumont, Fundamental of Radiochemistry, CRC Press, 1993</ref>

At the same time, he participated in the study of thermodynamic<ref>F David, K Samhoun, R. Guillaumont, N. Edelstein, «Thermodynamic properties of 5f elements », ''Journal of Inorganic and Nuclear Chemistry'', 1978, 40 (1), <abbr>p.</abbr> 69-74</ref><ref>R. Guillaumont (Chairman), T. Fanghänel, J. Fuger, I. Grenthe, V. Neck, D. Palmer, M. Rand,, Update on the Chemical Thermodynamics of Uranium, Neptunium, Plutonium, Americium and Technetium, AEN-OCDE, North- Holland,, Elsevier, 2003, 700 <abbr>p.</abbr></ref> and spectroscopic<ref>G. Ionova, J.C. Krupa, I. Gerard, R. Guillaumont, « Systematics in electron-transfer energies for lanthanides and actinides », ''New Journal of Chemistry'', 1995, 19 (5-6), <abbr>p.</abbr> 677-689</ref><ref>J.C. Krupa, M. Hussonnois, M. Genet, R. Guillaumont, « Optical spectra of Pa4+ diluted in ThCl4 single crystals », ''The Journal of Chemical Physics'', 1982,  77 (1), <abbr>p.</abbr> 154-158</ref> properties of elements 5f (and 4f) in connection with [[electronic transfers]] between these elements and their environment: covalence in two-phase solvent extraction systems and crystal field effect on solids, in particular single crystals examined at 4 K.

Finally, he continued his research on the fundamental problems of radionuclide migration in the environment<ref>B. Fourest, N. Hakem, R.  Guillaumont, « Characterization of colloids by measurement of their mobilities », ''Radiochimica Acta'', 1994, 66 (s1), <abbr>p.</abbr> 173-180</ref> (speciation, concentration effect, retention on [[colloid]]s) and selective separation of actinides/[[lanthanide]]s from the elements constituting spent nuclear fuel.<ref>G. Ionova, S. Ionov, C. Rabbe, C Hill, C. Madic, R. Guillaumont, J.C. Krupa, « Mechanism of trivalent actinide/lanthanide separation using bis (2, 4, 4-trimethylpentyl) dithiophosphinic acid (Cyanex 301) and neutral O-bearing co-extractant synergistic », ''Solvent Extraction and Ion Exchange'', 2001, 19 (3), <abbr>p.</abbr> 391-414</ref> R. Guillaumont's research themes are upstream of the many chemistry/radiochemistry problems encountered in "nuclear": chemistry of actinides from uranium to curium in the various stages of nuclear fuel cycles and radioactive waste management.

He has published more than 200 scientific articles, popular articles<ref>{{cite web|title=Actualités chimiques 1|url=https://www.lactualitechimique.org/spip.php?page=recherche&recherche=guillaumont|publication-date=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Actualité chimique 2|url=https://www.lactualitechimique.org/article_auteur/Guillaumont|publication-date=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Gestion des déchets radioactifs. R. Guillaumont. Techniques de l'Ingénieur, (2001) BN 3 660 et Doc BN 3 660 (2003) BN 3 661 et Doc BN 3 662|url=https://www.techniques-ingenieur.fr/base-documentaire/energies-th4/genie-nucleaire-ti180/|publication-date=}}</ref> and has written several books.<ref>{{cite web|title=BnF|url=https://catalogue.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/cb11906376c|publication-date=}}</ref>
